project.name: LumiNails
project.productType: beauty salon service and booking website

design.colorMode: light public UI; light and dark admin UI

typography.character: editorial serif with clear functional sans-serif UI

radius.hero: full-bleed desktop; 22px image card on mobile

motion.rule: transform and opacity only; respect prefers-reduced-motion

design.density: spacious public UI; compact admin workspace

must: Edit source CSS and rebuild generated bundles
Keep public and admin CSS ownership separate
Use semantic tokens and visible focus states
Keep mobile controls at least 44x44px and fields at least 16px
Read docs/design-system.md and docs/visual-audit.md before UI changes
avoid: Do not edit style.css or admin-v2.css directly
Do not use !important or duplicate override layers
Do not enable zoom in standalone admin PWA
Do not run tests in GitHub Actions
Do not use decorative glass or gradients without a functional reason
Do not introduce a new font family or radius tier

decisions.decision: Adopt a quiet-luxury editorial redesign for the TEST critical views.
decisions.reason: The user explicitly approved a redesign; the direction preserves LumiNails imagery and typography while improving hierarchy, booking clarity, contrast and responsive behavior.

decisions.decision: Use deep cacao as the primary action and dark showcase color, with warm ivory surfaces and muted blush accents.
decisions.reason: This keeps the beauty-studio character while providing stronger text and control contrast than the previous dusty rose primary.

decisions.decision: Treat the mobile hero image and gallery label as one framed card, and suppress the account recommendation when the hero already includes an account action.
decisions.reason: A single radius owner prevents broken nested corners, while removing the adjacent duplicate account promotion restores a clear homepage action hierarchy.

decisions.decision: Recolor the complete public and admin UI from the user-supplied five-color earth-neutral palette only.
decisions.reason: Cacao and ivory provide the accessible text/background extremes; blush, clay and caramel provide surfaces, borders and decorative hierarchy without changing layout or interaction.

decisions.decision: Assign the five palette colors distinct semantic roles instead of mapping most UI tokens to cacao.
decisions.reason: Ivory and lightly tinted blush carry readable content surfaces, clay and caramel define borders and supporting emphasis, and cacao remains the text and primary-action anchor.

decisions.decision: Use one shared 1240px content width and responsive section padding, while keeping the desktop home hero full-bleed.
decisions.reason: Introduction, services and gallery now align to the same gutters; the hero no longer clips its visual, and account and booking utility layouts retain desktop proportions.
